newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices down 1/4 to 3/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices down 1/4 to 3/8.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended 1/4 to 3/8 of a point lower as at least $350 million of bid lists pelted prices, traders said.
"It was pretty fast and furious for a while," a trader said.
Lists emanated mainly from bond funds and money managers for insurance companies, he said.

"It's a mixed bag," the trader said. "You look at some of the stuff that's out for the bid (and) you really couldn't get a pattern from what was going on. Some of the stuff had shorter calls, but some didn't. Some of it was nice, clean paper."
Given that munis have outperformed governments in recent weeks, some insurers may think tax-exempts are getting a little rich to Treasuries, he said.
"They might decide to buy another fixed income instrument," the trader said. "Maybe some people feel that Treasuries have a better opportunity to bounce back here."
Bond funds face the "same old story" of little cash, and are waiting to see how much redemption money flows back into municipals, he said.
It could also be that players just have a negative view on the market, the trader added.
"Sometimes people want to raise a little cash before the deals come, and don't forget too, you have some pretty explosive data coming out."
The markets receive December data on producer prices on Thursday and employment on Friday.
"And in our market trying to (sell on Wednesday) is too late," the trader said. "The day before the number the bid kind of gets weaker and fades."
The trader judged muni cash off by 3/8 to 1/2 point, mostly on the long end.

A municipal analyst described the broader market as down 1/4 to 3/8. High-grade issues ended flat to down 1/4 point, with top quality issues faring best. Dollar bonds ended down 1/4 to 3/8, he said. Bid lists aside, activity was light, he said.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract closed down 16/32 at 114-21/32. The March T-bond contract closed down 13/32 at 110-28/32. The MOB spread was 121 ticks.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed down 7/32 at 96-9/32 to yield 6.79 percent.

Turning to new issues, the JP Morgan said it won $150 million Washington general obligation bonds at a true interest cost of 5.534 percent. Bonds were reoffered to investors at top yield of 5.720 percent in 2022.

Lehman Brothers was named the winner of $96 million Washington motor vehicle fuel tax GOs after Merrill Lynch & Co's 5.55 percent TIC bid was rejected. Lehman was awarded the offering at a 5.56 TIC. Bonds were reoffered to investors at a top yield of 5.750 percent in 2022.

Also in competitive action, Merrill Lynch & Co won $80 million Delaware GO bonds at a 4.964 percent TIC. Bonds were reoffered to investors at a top yield of 5.45 percent in 2015. Bonds in the 2017 top maturity were not reoffered to investors.

On the negotiated side, Robinson-Humphrey Co Inc said it repriced and restructured Richmond County, Ga., Board of Education's $115 million bond offering. Yields were lowered in several maturities, but the top yield in 2026 remained unchanged at 5.95 percent.
Wednesday's scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales are expected to total $665 million in 31 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Competitive sales are expected to total $126 million in 19 issues. Negotiated sales total $539 million in 12 offerings.
